small_guidance:
- The post kernel is already trivial vs the ConvTranspose3d (which dominates at ~19ms). Tuning BLOCK_S/num_warps on `fused_post_kernel` will not move the needle; only fold bias into conv_transpose bias parameter to skip an op.
- If keeping the post kernel, try BLOCK_S=1024 with num_warps=4, num_stages=2, and a 2D grid over (N, spatial-tile) so the C=16 inner loop stays in registers.
- Pre-fold `self.bias` (scalar) by adjusting clamp bounds is fine, but the real cost is the conv_transpose; tuning here is a dead end.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose3d` with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile) computing the input×kernel outer product and atomically scattering into the output grid with stride=2/padding=1/output_padding handled in index math. This is where the ~19ms is spent.
- Alternative gather form: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile); for each output voxel, iterate IC × kD × kH × kW gathering only the input positions whose strided/padded index hits this output (i.e., (od+pad) % stride == 0 etc.). Channels-last (NDHWC) layout makes the IC reduction coalesced.
- Fuse the LogSumExp-over-C, HardSwish, bias-sub, and clamp directly into the convtranspose epilogue: have one program produce a full OC=16 vector for an output voxel in registers, run the LSE/HardSwish/clamp on the accumulator, and store a single fp32 — eliminating the intermediate [N,16,D',H',W'] tensor entirely.
